name: spritewright
description: A dependency-free pixel art editor: use it by itself in a browser or as a dependency of a game repo. Edits PNG sprites losslessly and can open a pull request with the changes.

paragraphs: A pixel art editor that works by itself in a browser or as a dependency inside a game repository. No runtime dependencies, no build step.

Tools. Brush sizes 1-16 (square or round tip) for the pencil, eraser, shade and the line and outline shapes; pencil with a "clean lines" pixel-perfect mode, eraser, fill (connected area or every pixel of that colour), line, rectangle and ellipse (outline or filled, Shift for squares, circles and 45° lines), a checkerboard dither pattern for the pencil, fills and shapes, a dither gradient (J: drag from the primary colour to the secondary, filling the selection or the area you start in with an ordered dither), a shade brush that steps colours lighter or darker with hue shifting (or through your…

Colour. Primary and secondary colours, under the tools: click the primary swatch for the colour popover (picker, hex, hue ramp, recolour), right next to where you draw (right click paints the secondary one, which starts out clear so right click erases; X swaps them; Z switches between pencil and eraser), hue-shifted 5-colour ramps you can add to the palette, recolour a colour everywhere, project palettes (.hex), palettes from Lospec by name or link (endesga-32), an Indexed mode (every picked colour snaps to the palette; double-click a palette colour to change it everywhere it is used in the…

whatItDoes.text: A pixel art editor that works by itself in a browser or as a dependency inside a game repository. No runtime dependencies, no build step.

requirements.text: Reading public repositories needs no sign-in at all.

To open private repositories and to send pull requests, the editor offers Sign in with GitHub: a popup on github.com (your normal login, SSO and 2FA included), then the editor can act on the repositories where the spritewright GitHub App is installed, with exactly three permissions (Contents, Pull requests and Issues, read and write; Issues is only for the Feedback button).

Artist with write access: a fine-grained personal access token limited to the game repository with Contents: read and write and Pull requests: read and write. (Reading a private repository in GitHub mode needs Contents: read too.)
